author: Mackenzie Web
title: California's wage law backfires… 18,000 jobs lost for hardworking Americans!
text:
The recent consequences of California’s $20 minimum wage law for fast-food workers serve as a stark reminder of the economic realities that hardworking Americans, particularly those of us over 60, have long understood. While politicians and progressive leaders tout such legislation as victories for the working class, the truth is clear: this policy has resulted in a loss of nearly 18,000 jobs. According to the National Bureau of Economic Research, California’s fast-food employment has decreased by 3.2 percent following the implementation of AB 1228, benefiting a political agenda rather than the very workers it intended to assist.
Many of us recall a time when hard work guaranteed a decent paycheck. We took pride in our jobs, which provided a pathway to stability and dignity. Today, we see government actions pushing us in the opposite direction. The decision by Governor Gavin Newsom and his fellow Democrats to impose such an unrealistic wage hike does nothing but strain businesses, lead to fewer available jobs, and ultimately create an environment where many hardworking individuals struggle to make ends meet.
While California’s fast-food sector is losing jobs, the rest of the nation is witnessing a modest increase. This discrepancy highlights the devastating effects of policies stemming from top-down ideologies that ignore the realities faced by small businesses. Our country has always prided itself on providing opportunities through hard work, yet progressive leadership in states like California is eroding that foundation with misguided wage control attempts. As noted by experts like Rachel Greszler of The Heritage Foundation, one cannot simply dictate wages without understanding the consequences that follow.
Moreover, it is disheartening to observe state officials denying the clear evidence before them. Instead of acknowledging their failed policies, they prefer to dismiss critical studies that challenge their narrative. This behavior demonstrates a systemic disconnect between politicians and the hardworking citizens they claim to serve.
For those of us who have dedicated our lives to labor, hard work, and perseverance, it is painful to watch our fellow Americans suffer due to decisions made far removed from reality. The job losses and economic hardships are not just statistics; they represent real people—friends, family members, and neighbors—seeking employment and security during troubling times. It is time to hold our leaders accountable and advocate for policies that prioritize the lives of ordinary Americans, rather than the ideological whims of the political elite. Let us stand united, always vigilant to ensure that our voices are heard and our hard work is honored.
